bull.b: Year-to-date revenue and unit growth indicate improving commercial traction despite quarterly volatility. Gains from Bellwright and ASA expand the portfolio’s contribution base, while higher volume can support continued investment in content and platform distribution over the next several quarters.

Meaningful installed bases and sustained daily engagement provide a durable foundation for live operations, downloadable content, and future monetization. Continued activity across PC, console, and mobile platforms gives Snail multiple opportunities to deepen player value and extend franchise lifecycles.

Higher cash improves near-term operating flexibility, while deferred revenue represents contracted or collected amounts tied to content still to be delivered. The sizable balance and planned DLC recognition provide greater revenue visibility, although execution remains necessary to convert that backlog.

bear.b: Negative equity reflects an impaired capital base and materially limits financial flexibility. It can increase dependence on external financing or balance-sheet actions, while also making the company more vulnerable if operating losses continue or cash generation weakens over the next several quarters.

The company has not yet demonstrated sustained operating profitability, and revenue has declined after a steep 2025 contraction. Losses reduce internally generated funding for new content, while uneven demand makes future earnings and cash conversion less predictable across reporting periods.

The conditional listing decision creates an ongoing structural constraint because Snail must rebuild equity and continue meeting disclosure and listing requirements. Failure to satisfy the condition could result in delisting, complicating access to public capital and increasing pressure on balance-sheet management.
